newsitem.title: UK: BARCLAYS EXTENDS GAINS, DKB UPGRADES.
newsitem.headline: BARCLAYS EXTENDS GAINS, DKB UPGRADES.

text.p: Barclays Plc shares extended their advance to about six percent as analysts prepared to upgrade their earnings estimates and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson upped the stock to "buy" from "add", market sources said.
By 0853 GMT, Barclays shares were up 77-1/2p at 14.05 stg after hitting a record high 14.15 stg in positive response to the bank's first-half earnings and buy-back news.
Analysts were expected to raise their estimates after meeting with the company this morning, traders said.
The bank's announcement that it would have greater than expected scope for share buy-backs this year and that first-half profits rose eight percent, boosted the shares initially, traders said.
Pre-tax profits rose to 1.376 billion pounds before one-off charges of 105 million sterling, against analysts' forecasts of between 1.216 and 1.347 billion.
"They were a splendid set of results and the buy-back news was pleasing," a trader said.
In an interview, chief executive Martin Taylor said its margins tightened in nearly every product area but it still managed a 30 percent rise in UK banking profits.
HSBC Holdings shares fell 12-1/2p to 22.92 stg, NatWest lost 5-1/2p to 836 stg and Abbey National rose 1-1/2p to 847p.
